chapter_theme: A song at Koonthalur (கூந்தலூர்): the poet heaps abuse on himself as a fool bound to women and asks that, even with one flower or leaf, he may fall at Murugan's feet in love; the praise names Rama, the peacock that lifts devotees, and Siva who calls Murugan guru.

874.reading: The poet calls himself a fool who has gone many ways on earth, a madman, a proud lump of a body without patience, an empty one fallen from greatness, a vagabond who left the path of penance, a sinner joined to scented-haired, moon-faced, net-eyed women, and asks for grace that, if not with many flowers then with one flower or one leaf, he may fall with love and worship Murugan's feet. The praise names Vishnu who with one arrow cut Ravana's ten heads and twenty arms as uncle, Murugan who dwells on the great peacock and gives the high state to devotees, poets, gods, sages and children, who raged until the whole clan of Suras who would not bow fell to dust, and whom Siva, holding the poison in his throat, calls guru, at Koonthalur.
874.nuance: வெகுமலர் அது கொடு வேண்டியாகிலும் ஒரு மலர் இலை கொடும்: the plea scales worship down to one flower or leaf offered with love, so the measure is love, not the offering. குருபரன் என வரு: Siva himself names Murugan guru. One word in the self-abuse (மீகுகேள்வி) is unclear.

links.note: Tirumular says anyone can give God a green leaf; 874 asks to worship with one flower or leaf if not many flowers. Both make the smallest offering enough, Tirumular as a duty open to all, 874 as a plea that love, not abundance, will be accepted.
